races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Havana Grey Star
runners_data.note: Prominent style with proven stamina at 6f, soft ground should suit, Jamie Spencer's tactical nous crucial
runners_data.comment: Looked a hard ride when coming off the bridle on Nottingham debut; can do better
runners_data.spotlight: 100-30 third favourite for her Nottingham debut 11 days ago (6f, good), a race where she travelled strongly but then looked an extremely difficult ride under pressure; possible that was just greenness and she can't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Halliwell Stream
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity on debut from yard in poor form, breeding suggests speed but unproven
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; 140,000gns yearling; first foal of a Group-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 92), herself closely related to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Queen Of Bermuda; stable, who also run Harlequin Sky, having first 2yo runners of the year; a newcomer of note.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Another Chapple-Hyam debutant with stamina breeding, yard's 1/12 record major concern
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 20,000gns breeze-up 2yo; ninth foal; half-sister to six winners including In The Breeze (1m2f/1m4f; RPR 91), He's A Rock Star (French 7f-1m5f including 2yo) and Allfredandnobell (2m-2m6f hurdle); dam unraced half-sister to 1m2f Group 1/Grade 1 winner Storming Home; one of two newcomers for Jane Chapple-Hyam.

runners_data.name: Sydney Grace
runners_data.note: Fellowes newcomer with decent breeding, trainer in better form but still speculative
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 40,000euros yearling; second foal; half-sister to 7f winner Teraabb (RPR 87); dam French/US 7f-8.5f winner (including 2yo/Listed; 100); stable have had a couple of winning 2yo newcomers this year; check the betting.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: Hold-up style worked at Newmarket, needs better tactical ride from Crouch
runners_data.comment: Hugely promising debut at Newmarket 17 days ago; leading claims with improvement likely
runners_data.spotlight: Lacked the professionalism, as much as the pace, of the three who beat her at Newmarket 17 days ago (5f, good to firm) but it was an encouraging debut with her greenness in mind; open to plenty of improvement; strong claims if coping with the slower ground.

runners_data.name: Minnie Bear
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter but faded badly on AW debut, 44 days off ring-rusty
runners_data.comment: Well-beaten last of eight on last month's Wolverhampton debut; longer-term prospect
runners_data.spotlight: Dropped right away to finish last of the eight runners on her Wolverhampton debut six weeks ago (5f; 22-1 into 14-1); needs to leave that well behind and probably a longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Sardinia
runners_data.note: Another pace angle but finished tailed off last time, tongue-tie addition noted
runners_data.comment: 33-1 when last of eight at Newmarket last month; now tried in a tongue tie
runners_data.spotlight: 33-1 when last of eight on her Newmarket debut (behind Havana Lightning) five weeks ago; now tongue tied; hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Havana Lightning
runners_data.note: Strong market support on debut suggests ability, hold-up style challenging in big field
runners_data.comment: Failed to justify strong favouritism on Newmarket debut; worth another chance
runners_data.spotlight: Only fifth of eight on her Newmarket debut last month (5f, good) but she was notably strong in the market that day (6-5 favourite) and the race looks a solid piece of form; surprising if she couldn't leave that well behind her in time.

runners_data.name: Sable Island
runners_data.note: Showed promise on AW, apprentice claim helpful but needs to handle turf transition
runners_data.comment: Promise amidst inexperience when 3rd at Southwell three weeks ago; others look stronger
runners_data.spotlight: Badly in need of the experience but shaped quite nicely when third of eight at Southwell three weeks ago (5f); should improve but others bring more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Alpaca's Bullet
runners_data.note: Poor debut effort suggests limited ability, needs major improvement from similar connections
runners_data.comment: Never dangerous when 8th of ten at Leicester 11 days ago (40-1); big step forward needed
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 for her recent Leicester debut (5f, good to firm), a race where she was hampered at the start before failing to threaten; needs to leave that well behind.

runners_data.name: Persian Sunset
runners_data.note: Modest Beverley third but has soft ground form, hold-up style suits if pace develops
runners_data.comment: Modest form when 3rd of five on debut at Beverley 16 days ago; can do better but needs to
runners_data.spotlight: Useful pedigree but ran to just a modest level when a 7l third of five at Beverley 16 days ago; open to improvement but it is a requirement.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Grey Star and Minnie Bear will likely lead early with Sea Of Sardinia also showing pace, creating a moderate tempo on the soft ground over this sharp 5f. The prominent runners should get an honest gallop without being burned off, while the hold-up horses like Havana Sprite, Havana Lightning and Sable Island will need to overcome traffic problems in a field of 11. The combination of testing ground conditions and a sustainable pace strongly favours prominent runners and those with proven form who can travel kindly in the first half of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent runners dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Grey Star and Minnie Bear set a steady tempo without killing each other
scenarios.body: The pace will be honest but not fierce, allowing horses racing handy to save energy for a finishing kick on ground that rewards stamina. Proven form horses with good tactical speed benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong between multiple pace-setters
scenarios.body: The soft ground will amplify the effects of early speed, setting up the race for closers who can stay widest and avoid trouble. Traffic will be crucial in a field this size.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants spring surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the newcomers from Jane Chapple-Hyam possess significant ability
scenarios.body: Halliwell Stream or Harlequin Sky could exploit the modest overall form level with natural talent on debut. The stable's poor recent record makes this unlikely but not impossible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If all the early leaders go too fast and tie up badly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole with any horse showing late pace capable of winning. This would require a serious pace miscalculation on testing ground.

watchPoints.text: Havana Grey Star could get an uncontested lead if Minnie Bear and Sea Of Sardinia both fail to show early pace
Traffic problems will be significant for hold-up horses like Havana Sprite and Havana Lightning in this field of 11
Jane Chapple-Hyam's runners Halliwell Stream and Harlequin Sky both represent market moves given stable's poor recent form
The soft ground conditions may not suit horses who showed their best form on faster surfaces
Several runners showing 44+ days since last run could need the outing despite the race conditions

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ardad Steve
runners_data.comment: 32,000gns yearling; first foal of a well-related maiden; betting useful on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 32,000gns yearling; first foal of a once-raced half-sister to winners Hadaatha (1m2f Listed) and Itlaaq (prolific 1m2f-2m), out of 1m Listed winner/1,000 Guineas third; stable have had a winning 2yo newcomer this year; betting to guide.

runners_data.name: Boysofwallstreet
runners_data.spotlight: 85,000gns foal, £95,000 yearling; fifth foal; brother to Group-placed 6f 2yo winner Pearl Glory (RPR 98), closely related to 6f/7f winner Guiteau (78); dam once-raced half-sister to Group-placed 6f/7f winner Louis The Pious; looks the part on paper and the betting should be revealing.

runners_data.name: Conciliate
runners_data.comment: 34,000gns yearling; dam a Listed sprint winner (RPR 104); betting to guide
runners_data.spotlight: 22,000gns foal, 34,000gns yearling; second foal of a 5f-6f winner (including Listed; RPR 104); stable yet to strike with 2yos (as of Monday) in 2026; betting to guide.

runners_data.name: Easy Answer
runners_data.comment: 70,000gns yearling; dam a maiden from family of top stayer Gildoran; likely best watched
runners_data.spotlight: 70,000gns yearling; second foal of a maiden from the family of top stayer Gildoran; stable's 2yos usually better for a run and likely best watched unless strong in the market.

runners_data.name: Peaceful Warrior
runners_data.comment: Brother to two winners out of well-related 2yo winner; stable's juveniles going well
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; brother to winners Brindi (US/Canadian 5f-7f including 2yo/Listed) and Boston Rose (French 7.5f turf 2yo/US 1m AW); dam 6f AW 2yo winner (RPR 83), sister to 6f Group 1 winner Emaraaty Ana; Kevin Ryan's juveniles have made a fast start to the season and he looks a strong contender.

runners_data.name: Rogue Imperial
runners_data.spotlight: 77,000gns yearling, 170,000gns breeze-up 2yo; second foal; half-brother to 7f 2yo winner Goodwood Galaxy (RPR 100); dam 7f/1m winner (77), half-sister to 7f 2yo (Moyglare Stud) and 1m (Irish 1,000 Guineas) Group 1 winner Fallen Angel; lots to like on paper and Archie Watson's 2yos have hit the ground running.

runners_data.name: Prince Kameo
runners_data.spotlight: 18-1 and in need of the experience on his Lingfield debut three weeks ago (6f, AW); can do better but such progress will be needed.

runners_data.name: Bassrah
runners_data.comment: Didn't live up to market billing on debut but still has time to do much better
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off the 9-2 third favourite for her debut at Nottingham last month (6f, good) but she ran green and never featured; should do better in time but there are some interesting newcomers for her to deal with today.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap

runners_data.name: Solanna
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 24-day break with headgear retained, needs clear run from back of field
runners_data.comment: Multiple winner, including C&D, and he arrives in good form; good or faster preferable
runners_data.spotlight: Nine wins to his name, including C&D, and just 1lb higher than for March's narrow Kempton success (1m3f); two creditable efforts have followed but he could use the ground drying out if he is to add to his tally.

runners_data.name: Dream Pirate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong course record on softer ground, trainer quiet recently but horse has winning form here
runners_data.comment: Two course wins (1m) and he has won over this trip on AW; one to take seriously
runners_data.spotlight: Two course wins on slower than good, the latest off 2lb lower last September; added a 1m2f success at Lingfield in January and his subsequent modest effort at Nottingham may have been needed after three-months off; more appealing than many.

runners_data.name: King's Hand
runners_data.note: Non-runner declared, was progressive type who would have been prominent in betting
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner for Sir Mark Prescott in January; two good runs to start off his time with Joseph Parr and he took a step forward when seeing off seven rivals at Lingfield on Monday (1m2f, good); more will be needed to defy a penalty but he's unexposed on turf and he can't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Jack Sparowe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse prone to slow starts, well handicapped but needs everything to fall right from rear
runners_data.comment: On a losing run but well treated and the change of headgear could give him a lift
runners_data.spotlight: On a losing run and can get it wrong at the start; well handicapped on 2025 best, however, and he stayed on for fourth at Newcastle 19 days ago; conditions shouldn't be an issue and he commands respect with new blinkers now replacing cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Goldie Trickett
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making handicap debut with Silvestre De Sousa booked, hooded first time suggests connections expect improvement
runners_data.comment: Fair third on stable/seasonal debut last month; steps up to 1m2f with stamina not assured
runners_data.spotlight: Some promise for William Haggas last year and again when third of ten on her stable/seasonal debut last month (1m, AW; hooded first time); this sister to her new yard's Group 1 1m winner Saffron Beach isn't sure to improve for the longer trip but she isn't fully exposed just yet.

runners_data.name: Law Supreme
runners_data.note: Only front-runner in field with Billy Loughnane back aboard, can control race from flag fall
runners_data.comment: Had an excuse last time and his record for Billy Loughnane makes him of some interest
runners_data.spotlight: His good run of form ground to a halt at Thirsk last time but he can be given a pass as he was tight for room at a crucial stage; Billy Loughnane back on board today and his record for him reads 4111; one to take seriously.

runners_data.name: Special Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare stepping up in trip, has shown promise in recent handicaps at shorter distances
runners_data.comment: Two encouraging handicap runs last month; step up to 1m2f could unlock further progress
runners_data.spotlight: She has not been beaten far in two handicaps at around 1m this spring, keeping on for a 2l fifth at Southwell three weeks ago; still has some potential and stepping up to 1m2f could unlock it.

runners_data.name: Urban Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 128-day absence, showed promise in handicap debut at longer trip
runners_data.comment: Improved when 4th on handicap debut in January (1m6f, AW); hood left off today; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three maiden/novice runs but there was more promise to be gleaned from his handicap debut fourth at Wolverhampton (1m6f, AW; well supported) in January, a race where he still looked to be learning his craft; the hood worn on that occasion is now dispensed with; capable of better.

races.paceDynamic: Law Supreme stands alone as the only natural front-runner in this 8-runner field, meaning he can dictate proceedings unchallenged through the early stages. With seven hold-up horses behind him, this creates a tactical nightmare as they'll all be looking for racing room in the straight. The moderate early pace will see the field bunch up turning for home, before a frantic sprint develops over the final 2-3 furlongs. This race shape heavily favours the early leader Law Supreme, who can steal a march while the pack sorts itself out behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Law Supreme Steals March
scenarios.trigger: If Law Supreme gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lone front-runner can open up a decisive advantage while seven hold-up horses get in each other's way behind. By the time they organize a challenge, Law Supreme may have built an unassailable lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their runs perfectly despite traffic problems
scenarios.body: The bunched field produces a sustained finish where class tells and the best horse gets through. Superior tactical jockeys like De Sousa find the gaps that matter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Law Supreme goes too slow early and gets swamped by the field
scenarios.body: The crawling pace becomes a sprint finish where every horse has a chance. The best turn of foot wins in a blanket finish over the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites get blocked while an unfancied runner finds clear daylight
scenarios.body: Multiple interference incidents help a well-positioned outsider who avoids the trouble. An each-way surprise emerges from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Law Supreme breaking smoothly from stalls - if he misses the start, the entire pace scenario changes
Traffic problems in home straight with seven hold-up horses needing room - multiple interference likely
Goldie Trickett's hood application first time suggests stable expects significant improvement
Jack Sparowe's starting manners given his record of getting it wrong at flag fall
Billy Loughnane's return to Law Supreme after missing last ride - trainer clearly values the partnership

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap

runners_data.name: Saratoga Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed good form at end of 2024 and ran positively on reappearance 18 days ago over shorter trip
runners_data.comment: On losing run but mark is in range & shaped okay on his return; drying ground would help
runners_data.spotlight: Losing run stretches back to July 2023 but he ended 2025 in good form and his reappearance at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) 18 days ago was a positive one; stepping back up in distance is a positive but he could do with the ground drying out.

runners_data.name: Golden Garden
runners_data.note: Made all to win over this distance last September, has headgear fitted and returns from hurdles with Warren Greatrex showing decent recent form
runners_data.comment: 1m6f AW win for Jamie Osborne; solid 4th back on Flat 19 days ago; contender down in class
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to win a 1m6f handicap at Wolverhampton for Jamie Osborne last September; unplaced in two hurdle runs for this yard but he didn't run badly returned to the Flat at Goodwood 19 days ago (1m6f, good); down in class today and should have a big run in him.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse
runners_data.note: Won easily at Southwell over this trip off much lower mark, two recent seconds suggest he's in good heart
runners_data.comment: Two solid efforts at Southwell last month; seems fully effective on turf; in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Ran away with a Class 6 handicap at Southwell last October (1m6f) off a 10lb lower mark; two runner-up finishes at Southwell last month (after a 166-day absence) and he seemed fully effective on turf last year; one to take seriously.

runners_data.name: Dereham
runners_data.note: Previously won this very race in 2021, long absence of 244 days is concerning despite past course success
runners_data.comment: Won this race in 2021 and 2nd in it last year; may come on for this after eight months out
runners_data.spotlight: Shed his maiden tag in the corresponding race in 2021 (good to soft) and he has added a further four wins, the last three in consecutive renewals of a 2m handicap at Newmarket; chased home a stablemate in this race last year after a six-month absence; back from eight months off today and perhaps vulnerable to younger legs.

runners_data.name: Relocal
runners_data.note: Only front runner in field, new stable debut for Dylan Cunha who has solid strike rate, unproven on turf
runners_data.comment: Chance on best form for R Varian; more to prove on turf but not discounted on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: The winner of one of his 11 starts for Roger Varian, namely a 13.3f handicap at Chelmsford in January; sold for 8,500gns last month; still to prove as good on turf as AW but that is perhaps circumstance, rather than a marked preference for artificial surfaces.

runners_data.name: Iwantmytimewithyou
runners_data.note: Won two handicaps last July, recent form includes two seconds suggesting he's close to winning again
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in two of his three starts this year but could do with the rain staying away
runners_data.spotlight: Won two handicaps last July (1m4f, good and 1m6f, firm); he has finished second in two of his three runs this year, latterly beaten a short-head at Leicester 11 days ago (1m4f, good to firm); had just one run on slower than good and finished well beaten, so conditions may be a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Relocal is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should get an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop over this staying trip. With all other runners showing hold-up tendencies, there's no early pace pressure expected, allowing Relocal to dictate terms from the front. The lack of prominent racers means those tracking will need to time their challenges perfectly from mid-division or further back. This race shape strongly favours the lone pace-setter Relocal, who can control the tempo and potentially steal a march on the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Relocal Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Relocal gets an easy lead and maintains a steady tempo without being challenged early
scenarios.body: The front runner can quicken at the right moment while the hold-up horses struggle to close the gap having given him too much rope. George Wood can dictate exactly when to up the ante from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their challenges to perfection and Relocal's stamina gives way
scenarios.body: The pace becomes a tactical crawl which suits the closers who can produce their best turn of foot in the final two furlongs. Betelgeuse and Saratoga Gold have the class to overhaul a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Early Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses decides to race closer to Relocal and applies some pressure
scenarios.body: This creates a more honest gallop that could find out Relocal's stamina reserves while still allowing the better stayers to mount challenges. The improved pace helps horses like Dereham who needs a strong tempo over this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If Relocal goes too slow early and multiple horses make their moves simultaneously in a bunched finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint where positioning and luck matter more than class or form. Any horse can win in a blanket finish but jockey skills become paramount.

watchPoints.text: Relocal gets too soft a lead early - if no horse tracks him within 3-4 lengths through the first mile he could steal this
Betelgeuse's jumping from the weights at 133lbs after winning off 58 at Southwell - the handicapper may have him sussed
Dereham's fitness after 244 days off - any signs of hard blowing or sweating up would be concerning
Golden Garden's headgear change to tongue-tie - suggests connections are trying something different after hurdles stint
How quickly the field bunches up behind Relocal in the back straight - early positioning will be crucial in small field

races.name: Download The At The Races App Handicap

runners_data.name: Kamaway
runners_data.note: Won well here last week but hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage with weak early pace on testing ground
runners_data.comment: Impressive over C&D last week (good to soft); well in under a penalty; major player
runners_data.spotlight: Unable to justify favouritism on her handicap debut in March (7f, AW) but she showed her true colours with a comfortable C&D win (good to soft) last week; well in under her penalty and she has more to offer; solid claims.

runners_data.name: Lastchancezouloon
runners_data.note: Long absence and stable out of form but drop in class and step up in trip could help hold-up type
runners_data.comment: New trip/headgear offer hope of better on stable debut but others look far more persuasive
runners_data.spotlight: Bits of form for Richard Fahey but she finished down the field in two runs for Jack Channon in late 2025; sold for 1,000gns in January; upped in trip and tried in a hood on her stable debut.

runners_data.name: Havana Tobouggaloo
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid recent Bath second but needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Fine 2nd on seasonal return last month; up 3lb but still looks a leading contender
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on a couple of occasions last season and she ran to a higher level on her seasonal return, going down narrowly in a 1m handicap at Bath last month (1m, good to soft); the winner there has followed up since and the pair were well clear of the third so a 3lb rise looks justified; solid contender.

runners_data.name: Emery Down
runners_data.note: Hold-up style and trainer struggling for winners makes task tough despite stable switch
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but her best form has come on AW and others hold stronger claims
runners_data.spotlight: Of interest on her best AW efforts for John Butler and her second run for this yard was better than her first; needs another step forward if she is to come out on top and still has a bit to prove on the grass.

runners_data.name: Timely Affair
runners_data.note: Beat Ribston Pippin last time but hold-up style not ideal for weak pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Improved for cheekpieces with ready AW win latest; up 6lb but could have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Steady progress since handicapping and he took his form to a new level with his ready defeat of Ribston Pippin at Southwell three weeks ago (1m, AW; cheekpieces first time); up 6lb but open to further progress and he should go well if the ground is suitable (smart half-sister Royal Velvet happiest on good or faster).

runners_data.name: Tilani
runners_data.note: Fresh from Newbury win with good tactical speed to overcome hold-up classification
runners_data.comment: Unpenalised for his ready Class 5 win last week (1m, good); obvious chance of following up
runners_data.spotlight: Galway winner for Dermot Weld last summer; first win for new stable (third attempt) when comfortably seeing off 12 rivals at Newbury last week (1m, good) and he escapes a penalty for that apprentice-race success; of obvious interest dropped into a Class 6.

runners_data.name: Ribston Pippin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form gives tactical edge in weak pace scenario
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; second to Timely Affair latest; 4lb turnaround may be insufficient though
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner last summer (good to firm) and he added to his haul with a ready win at Southwell (1m, AW) in December; chased home Timely Affair back at Southwell three weeks ago (1m) but while he is 4lb better off today, he wouldn't be sure to reverse the placings (raced awkwardly under pressure).

runners_data.name: Charming Fellow
runners_data.note: Long absence but prominent style suits race shape if fitness holds up
runners_data.comment: Quiet for new yard (AW) but may prove a different proposition back on turf; check betting
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Pontefract nursery for Peter Chapple-Hyam in October 2024 (1m, soft); in good form last autumn too but he has been sent off at big prices and finished down the field in three runs for his new stable this year; could prove a different proposition back on turf, especially if the going remains on the slow side, and cheekpieces return today; check betting.

runners_data.name: Poke The Bear
runners_data.note: Three AW wins but returning to turf where previously well held creates doubt
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW over the winter but below par on last three runs; more to prove on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins at Lingfield (7f-1m) over the winter; his form has cooled more recently and he returns to turf (well held in one attempt) with a point to prove; can blow the start.

runners_data.name: Cezarro
runners_data.note: Cheekpieces applied and consistent recent efforts give each-way hope at big price
runners_data.comment: 12-race maiden but running well since joining current yard; each-way shout back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: 0-12 but he has shown winning potential since joining Ross Burdon, including a second of nine at Kempton in March; each-way shout now back on turf with cheekpieces returning.

races.paceDynamic: Ribston Pippin will set the early tempo from his prominent position, with Charming Fellow likely to sit just behind him in second. The pace will be moderate and sustainable given the lack of natural speed in this field and the soft ground conditions. Most runners are hold-up horses who will need to find their way into the race from off the pace, creating a bunched field turning for home. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed, as the lack of early pace will make it difficult for back-markers to pick up the pieces in testing ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace becomes crawling and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine early speed allows the field to bunch up, creating a cavalry charge where horses with tactical pace and good recent form prosper. Hold-up horses with finishing kicks struggle to get into contention from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ribston Dominates Front
scenarios.trigger: If Ribston Pippin gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: His prominent style pays dividends as he controls the tempo throughout and has enough left to repel late challenges on ground that suits. The pace-setter's advantage becomes decisive when the field struggles to close from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground really bites and stamina becomes the key factor
scenarios.body: The testing conditions favour horses with proven staying power who can grind out a finish over this trip. Recent winners with momentum find another gear when others tire in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite Kamaway fails to reproduce last week's form and the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop sets up a messy finish where an improving horse at big odds can steal through on the rails or wide. Form horses disappoint and value emerges from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Ribston Pippin gets soft lead and kicks clear turning in - field may not catch him in testing ground
Monitor pace development early - if crawling tempo develops it will disadvantage all hold-up horses severely
Check market moves on Cezarro who could outrun odds if recent Kempton second form translates to turf
Watch for Kamaway being produced too late if pace collapses - may not have time to use finishing kick
Observe Timely Affair's position turning in - needs to be closer than usual given weak pace setup

runners_data.name: Giorgio M
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 21-day break, benefits from regular jockey booking and trainer's 1/20 recent record
runners_data.comment: On a good mark, 4lb lower than for his close 2nd in this race last year; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to win a 7f AW handicap at Lingfield in December, his second start for Mark Loughnane; in and out since that success but no doubt he is handicapped to go well and he has run well over C&D in the past (including finishing second in this race year off 4lb higher); one to consider with Billy Loughnane back in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Tactical Plan
runners_data.note: Proven soft ground performer with two wins on slow surfaces, prominent style suits if pace develops
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice on slow ground in the autumn of 2024; in and out in his three runs this year but his Leicester fourth last month (7f, good) brings him into the reckoning; a visor is now tried (ran well in one attempt in cheekpieces); further rainfall would aid his chance.

runners_data.name: Tennessee Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to optimum 7f trip off reduced mark, 44-day absence not ideal
runners_data.comment: Won three times in 2024 but drawn a blank since; drops in class and back to optimum trip
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins in 2024 but he has drawn a blank since; returns to his optimum trip off a reduced mark and this is his first Class 5 handicap for some time; not solid but he has the ability to go well.

runners_data.name: Welljudged
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare making turf debut from all-weather racing, low mileage asset but question marks
runners_data.comment: Not kicked on in handicaps as yet; switches to turf with a career best required
runners_data.spotlight: Hit the frame in her first three starts last autumn; handicaps have proved more troublesome but she still has low mileage and today's switch to turf could give her a lift.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner recently switched to Adam Kirby stable, 30-day gap manageable
runners_data.comment: Has been rated a fair bit higher in the past; betting to guide starting out for Adam Kirby
runners_data.spotlight: The winner of three of his 34 starts for Richard Fahey, the latest off this mark at Newcastle in January (6f); sold for 19,000gns last month; capable at this level and the betting should be revealing starting out for Adam Kirby.

runners_data.name: Chilly Breeze
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with 279-day layoff major concern despite low career mileage
runners_data.comment: 5f win as a 2yo; quiet last year; low mileage but likely best watched on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Early-season 5f win as a 2yo when trained by David Evans; unplaced in two handicap runs last summer; still has low mileage and it will be interesting to see how he goes in the market prior to this stable debut (same owners).

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist coming off C&D second on soft ground just 7 days ago
runners_data.comment: All wins on AW but fully effective on turf; solid second over C&D last week; considered
runners_data.spotlight: His three wins have all come at Kempton (7f/1m) but he is fully effective on turf, runner-up over C&D (soft) last week; won't be far away with a repeat.

runners_data.name: Rogue Allegiance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner switching to Jack Jones stable with solid recent Leicester second
runners_data.comment: Two promising runs for his new yard this spring; handicapped to win; slower than good a ?
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't kick on from his winning debut for David O'Meara; down in the weights as a result and he has run two solid races for his new stable, second over 6f at Leicester last month before a good third over C&D four weeks ago (good to firm); untried on slower than good but handicapped to win.

runners_data.name: Middleton View
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 49-day break, last win came at 5f which raises trip concerns
runners_data.comment: 5f AW win on stable debut in December; little to cheer since and now steps back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: He made a winning start for Stuart Williams when strong at the finish over 5f at Chelmsford in December; little to cheer since and hopes are pinned on the return to 7f/turf having a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Uppercase
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 43-day absence, showed promise at 8f+ which questions today's 7f trip
runners_data.comment: Promising start to career but his last two runs have seen his form dip; still low mileage
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in maiden/novice company and again when second of nine on his handicap debut at Pontefract last summer (1m, good); below that level two weeks later and again on his return to action six weeks ago; now has a point to prove but still brings low mileage.

runners_data.name: Noble Guest
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with two C&D wins last season, just 7 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Two C&D wins last year; promising return last month before a low-key run on soft last week
runners_data.spotlight: Two C&D wins (good and good to soft) last year and he comes here just 2lb higher than for the latter success; promising reappearance last month but he failed to fire on soft ground here last week; type to bounce back.

races.paceDynamic: Chilly Breeze is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms uncontested through the early stages at Yarmouth's 7f trip. With prominent runners Giorgio M, Tactical Plan, Ziggy's Condor and Noble Guest likely settling just behind, the pace will be sustainable rather than fierce. The large contingent of hold-up horses including Berry Clever, Tennessee Gold, Welljudged, Rogue Allegiance, Middleton View and Uppercase will be relying on the tempo staying honest to launch late challenges. This race shape strongly favours the patient hold-up horses who can exploit the expected steady gallop and finish fastest when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Chilly Breeze sets a sedate pace unchallenged through halfway
scenarios.body: The tempo will be too slow for the prominent runners to sustain their kicks, allowing the back-markers to unleash devastating late runs. Berry Clever and Tennessee Gold are perfectly positioned to capitalise with their proven finishing power.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pressure tells
scenarios.trigger: If Giorgio M or Tactical Plan press Chilly Breeze early to inject pace
scenarios.body: The increased gallop will set up perfectly for the prominent brigade who can sustain their effort to the line. Giorgio M's recent Lingfield win and Tactical Plan's soft ground form make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sole leader survives
scenarios.trigger: If Chilly Breeze gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: Despite the 279-day layoff, his low mileage and proven front-running ability could see him hold off late challengers. The soft ground suits based on his juvenile win under similar conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo becomes crawling with no pressure applied anywhere
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where the highest-rated horses with tactical speed prevail. Tennessee Gold's class edge and Noble Guest's recent form could prove decisive in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Chilly Breeze could steal this if given uncontested lead - watch for any early pressure from Giorgio M or Tactical Plan
Berry Clever ran second here 7 days ago on identical conditions - quick turnaround could be positive or negative
Tennessee Gold drops to Class 5 company for first time in months off 44-day break - market support crucial
Noble Guest carries 3lb apprentice allowance which effectively puts him on same mark as last year's C&D wins
Watch early positioning of Giorgio M and Tactical Plan - if they let Chilly Breeze bowl along unchallenged the hold-up horses benefit massively
